text.div:
SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD

  • Nephrology consultation for reduced kidney function (race-free eGFR 38) with albuminuria of uncertain cause, a 5-year kidney failure risk above 5% if the disease proves chronic, and APOL1 genetic counseling
  • Confirm and stage the kidney disease: race-free eGFR from creatinine with cystatin C, repeat urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio, urinalysis with microscopy, kidney ultrasound, a monoclonal protein screen (serum protein electrophoresis and free light chains), hepatitis B, hepatitis C and HIV tests, and any earlier results she can obtain
  • Blood pressure: a validated home monitor with readings twice a day for seven days to confirm the diagnosis; sodium below 2 g a day; recheck in two weeks
  • Stop over-the-counter naproxen and use acetaminophen for knee aching; avoid all NSAIDs; tell every clinician and pharmacist about her kidneys before new medicines or contrast dye
  • Anemia and mineral and bone checks: hemoglobin with iron studies, calcium, phosphate, intact PTH and 25-hydroxyvitamin D at baseline
  • Baseline ECG, TSH for tiredness, a lipid panel once at diagnosis, A1c to screen for diabetes, and a PHQ-9
  • On the nephrologist's advice: losartan 50 mg daily with potassium and creatinine in two weeks, then dapagliflozin 10 mg daily with a further check at two to four weeks, then losartan increased to the highest dose tolerated; sick-day rules for both; atorvastatin 20 mg; vitamin D3 1,000 units daily with PTH and vitamin D again at three months; blood pressure goal below 130/80 and a systolic below 120 if tolerated
  • APOL1 genetic testing offered after counseling on what a result would and would not change, on privacy, and on what it could mean for relatives; her decision to defer recorded, with the offer left open
  • Kidney education session on the kidneys and the treatment options if they fail (transplant, home and center dialysis, and conservative kidney management), long before any decision is needed; kidney diet session with the dietitian
  • Vaccines for chronic kidney disease: high-dose influenza, PCV20 and two doses of HepB-CpG (she was not immune), then RSV, recombinant zoster and COVID-19, spaced at her request
  • Dapagliflozin 10 mg daily started now that potassium and creatinine are stable on losartan
  • Losartan increased to 100 mg; potassium and creatinine in two to four weeks; urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio, hemoglobin, PTH and vitamin D at three months on treatment; nephrology review at three months

resource.title: Ida B. Wells synthetic care plan
resource.description: Chronic kidney disease found in time in a 68-year-old Black woman, a journalist and civic leader in Chicago, who comes in tired with swollen ankles. The teaching contrast is her documented death from kidney failure after a brief illness: here the disease is found, staged and treated years before kidney failure. The episode covers the race-free CKD-EPI 1926 equations (creatinine, then creatinine with cystatin C) and the history of race-based eGFR delaying the recognition and referral of Black patients, as the NKF-ASN Task Force described; staging on the KDIGO 1929 heat map with the urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio and the kidney failure risk equation; finding the cause (home blood pressure, diabetes screening, urinalysis, kidney ultrasound, and a monoclonal protein screen); APOL1 genetic testing offered with counseling and left to her choice; an ARB and an SGLT2 inhibitor with potassium and creatinine checks; blood pressure control; a statin; stopping naproxen; anemia and mineral and bone checks; vaccinations; a nephrology consultation; and shared decisions about kidney replacement options should the disease progress, under the KDIGO 1929 guideline, the 1930 AHA/ACC blood pressure guideline and the CMID chronic kidney disease monograph.
